bank.genesis_capital_note: The bank opens holding this reserve, capitalised from SYS-MARKET at economy setup with reason 'bank_capital' (a recorded genesis ledger row, like population seed balances). GDD-03 §4.3: the bank lends only what it holds — disbursements are capped by the SYS-BANK balance.
bank.min_reserve_note: Crisis detection watches reserves / outstanding loans against this floor (SIM MODEL threshold).

business.note: A business may hire only while its balance covers wage_reserve_months of its wage bill (SIM MODEL prudence rule). A business that cannot meet its obligations for distress_months_to_closure consecutive months closes, with recorded consequences.

crisis_thresholds.note: SIM MODEL detection thresholds. A crisis opens only on measured indicator breaches, never on a dice roll; it resolves after two consecutive months back inside the threshold.

notes: Session 04 economy configuration. Canonical rates stay where the design put them: income tax brackets, the 8% business tax and the 0.5% property tax live in prices.json 'tax' (GDD-03 §4.2), and loan/savings rates live in prices.json 'loans' (GDD-03 §4.3-4.4) — this file REFERENCES them, never copies them. Rates that exist only here are new Session 04 lines with no design-data basis; each is marked SIM MODEL and labelled wherever it surfaces.
scenarios_note: Configurable exogenous shocks, fired deterministically by month_index: entries like {"type": "demand_shock", "month_index": 6, "duration_months": 2, "takings_factor": 0.6}. Empty by default — no shock is invented for the standard world.

tax_rules.import_tariff_note: SIM MODEL rate (no tariff exists in the design data). Charged on intercity trade flow value, paid from the SYS-MARKET clearing account to SYS-CITY with reason 'tariff'.
tax_rules.sales_tax_note: SIM MODEL rate (no sales tax exists in the design data). Applied as a split of household market purchases at settlement: the household pays exactly what it paid before; the tax share is routed to SYS-CITY with reason 'sales_tax' instead of to SYS-MARKET.
